title: Upper weight of a Fourier partner
statement:
Let $\psi$ be a nontrivial additive character of $k_0$ [def-fd-additive-character]. Let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion and let
$\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$, with no
geometric irreducible constituent [def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] isomorphic to
$\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$ for any $a\in k$, including $a=0$, and punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$ [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let
$j':U'_0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion and
let $\mathcal M'$ be a lisse Weil sheaf on $U'_0$ such that the Fourier–Deligne transform [def-fd-transform] of the middle extension [def-wf-middle-extension] satisfies
\[
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')[1],
\]
and suppose that $\mathcal M'$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of some real
weight $v$. Then $v\le w+1$.

source.place: The Fourier upper weight proposition, order 3121

proof.text: Apply [prop-fd-zero-extension-comparison] to the given Fourier-partner isomorphism. Its hypotheses are precisely the nontriviality of $\psi$, nonzero Weil irreducibility and constituent-nonexceptionality of $\mathcal M$, and its punctual purity of weight $w$; geometric irreducibility and unramifiedness at infinity are unnecessary. The complement of $U_0$ is finite: a proper closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}k_0[x]$ is the zero set of a nonzero polynomial and has finitely many closed points. Obtain $\mathcal G,\mathcal B'$ with $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!\mathcal M[1])\cong\mathcal G[1]$ and $0\to\mathcal B'\to\mathcal G\to j'_*\mathcal M'\to0$, where $\mathcal B'$ is lisse on the entire dual line and its closed-point eigenvalues satisfy $|\iota\alpha|^2\le q_y^w$. Put $r=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal M>0$ and $b=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal B'\ge0$. Ranks are constant on the connected opens in question, by the finite-rank local trivializations in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves].

source.place: First paragraph: introduce the correction and its ranks

proof.text: Fix $n\ge1$ and $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, $X_0\in\{U_0,A'_0\}$, above a closed point $y$ of degree $e$; then $e\mid n$. Restrict to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ (a Weil pullback by [prop-weil-operations]; same point and Weil iterates, hence the same stalk operators). By [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] represent the object, its Weil map and inverse at one finite stage $E$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]; on each geometric component [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] identifies the sheaf with a finite-dimensional $E$-space, and a basis gives a free lattice whose reductions are finite free in degree $0$, so of finite Tor dimension. This is the integral representative required by [lem-trf-rational-local-frobenius-powers]; take as starting lift the geometric point $\bar y$ defining $F_y$. That lemma makes the normalized operator at $x$ conjugate to the $(n/e)$-th power of the normalized operator at $\bar y$. By [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization] the point transport of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] equals the scheme-Frobenius transport, so after composing with the iterated Weil map both normalized operators are those of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]: $F^{(n)}_x$ is conjugate to $F_y^{n/e}$, also after extension to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. By [p-linear-triangular] choose a basis adapted to an $F_y$-invariant full flag; the diagonal entries of $F_y^{n/e}$ are $\alpha_i^{n/e}$, so by [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] its trace is their sum. For $\mathcal M$, [def-weil-punctual-weights] gives $|\iota\alpha_i|=q^{ew/2}$; for $\mathcal B'$ Step 1 gives $\le$. The triangle inequality gives $|\iota t_{\mathcal M,n}(x)|\le rq^{nw/2}$ on $U_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and $|\iota t_{\mathcal B',n}(x)|\le bq^{nw/2}$ on $A'_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, including repeated eigenvalues, nonsemisimple Frobenius and $b=0$.

source.place: First and second paragraphs: bounds for the two trace functions

proof.text: Set $K=(j_!\mathcal M)[1]$. To compute its trace function in the adic coefficient category, apply the arbitrary compact-support base-change clause of [prop-functor-package] to the open immersion $j$ and each geometric point of the line. The fibre of $j$ is that point when it lies in $U$, and is empty otherwise, so the fibre of $j_!\mathcal M$ is the fibre of $\mathcal M$ in the first case and the zero complex in the second (direct image for the identity, respectively for the empty source). These are comparisons on $D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, not an assertion about discrete rational coefficients on the small etale site. The Weil-equivariance clause of [prop-weil-operations] makes them commute with the local return Frobenius. By the alternating-trace definition [def-fd-trace-function], shifting a sheaf by $[1]$ negates its trace. Thus $t_{K,n}(x)=-t_{\mathcal M,n}(x)$ for $x\in U_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and $t_{K,n}(x)=0$ otherwise. There are exactly $q^n$ points of the affine line, identified with the elements of $\mathbf F_{q^n}$ by their coordinate. Step 2 consequently gives $\sum_{x\in A_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})}|\iota t_{K,n}(x)|^2\le r^2 q^{n(w+1)}$.

source.place: First paragraph: zero-extension trace function and point count

proof.text: Apply [cor-fd-plancherel] to $K$ of Step 3. By Step 1 its transform is $\mathcal G[1]$, whose trace is $-t_{\mathcal G,n}$ by [def-fd-trace-function]. Squaring removes this sign, so $\sum_{y\in A'_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})}|\iota t_{\mathcal G,n}(y)|^2=q^n\sum_{x\in A_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})}|\iota t_{K,n}(x)|^2\le r^2q^{n(w+2)}$. Also the bound on $\mathcal B'$ from Step 2 and the same point count give $\sum_{y\in A'_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})}|\iota t_{\mathcal B',n}(y)|^2\le b^2q^{n(w+1)}$.

source.place: First two displayed estimates: Plancherel and the correction energy

proof.text: For a closed point $y$ of $U'_0$, apply [lem-wf-rational-stalk-exact] to the short exact sequence in Step 1. On $U'_0$ its last sheaf restricts to $\mathcal M'$: by the sections formula of [def-wf-middle-extension], $V\times_{A'_0}U'_0=V$ for $V$ over $U'_0$. Thus the stalk sequence is $0\to\mathcal B'_{\bar y}\to\mathcal G_{\bar y}\to\mathcal M'_{\bar y}\to0$, with commuting Frobenius. A basis of the subspace extended by lifts of a quotient basis makes the Frobenius matrix block upper triangular, with the subspace and quotient matrices on its diagonal. Every positive power has the corresponding powers as diagonal blocks. Summing diagonal entries by [def-weil-endomorphism-trace] and using, for each of $\mathcal B',\mathcal G,\mathcal M'$ at each rational point, the conjugacy $F^{(n)}_x\sim F_y^{n/e}$ obtained exactly as in Step 2 (restriction to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$, free lattice, [lem-trf-rational-local-frobenius-powers] and [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization]) therefore gives $t_{\mathcal M',n}(y)=t_{\mathcal G,n}(y)-t_{\mathcal B',n}(y)$ for every $y\in U'_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$. No splitting of the Weil-sheaf sequence is asserted.

source.place: Third paragraph: trace additivity on the partner open

proof.text: For complex $a,c$, $|a-c|^2\le(|a|+|c|)^2\le2|a|^2+2|c|^2$, since $(|a|-|c|)^2\ge0$. Apply this to Step 5 and sum. All summands are nonnegative, so the sums over $U'_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ are bounded by those over the whole dual line in Step 4. Consequently $S_n(U'_0,\mathcal M')\le2r^2q^{n(w+2)}+2b^2q^{n(w+1)}\le2(r^2+b^2)q^{n(w+2)}$. The last inequality uses $q>1$ and $q^{n(w+1)}=q^{n(w+2)}q^{-n}\le q^{n(w+2)}$, valid for every real $w$. The constant $C=2(r^2+b^2)$ is positive because $r>0$, and independent of $n$.

source.place: Third paragraph: squared difference and the uniform exponential bound

proof.text: The given $\mathcal M'$ is nonzero. Indeed, if it were zero, its ordinary direct image would be zero, so the assumed isomorphism would give $\operatorname{FT}_\psi((j_*\mathcal M)[1])=0$. Apply the inverse-character transform and [lem-fd-inversion] in rank one to obtain $((j_*\mathcal M)[1])(-1)=0$. The Tate line is locally free of rank one at integral coefficients by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3), and [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] carries it and its dual to the rational/common-stage categories. Locally the evaluation of the line tensored with its dual is multiplication of scalars and is an isomorphism, so tensoring by the two lines gives mutually inverse functors. Shift is also invertible. Hence $j_*\mathcal M=0$. Restriction back to $U_0$ is $\mathcal M$ by the sections formula of [def-wf-middle-extension], contradicting the hypothesis $\mathcal M\ne0$. Here the transform takes zero to zero because it is an exact triangulated functor by [def-fd-transform].

source.place: Final paragraph: nonvanishing of the prescribed Fourier partner

proof.text: The dense open $U'_0$ is a smooth geometrically connected affine curve: its finite complement in $\operatorname{Spec}k_0[x]$ is cut out by a product $f$ of distinct irreducible polynomials, so $U'_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0[x,1/f]$ (take $f=1$ for empty complement). Over any field extension the coordinate $x$ lifts across a nilpotent quotient and $f(x)$ remains a unit, proving the infinitesimal lifting property; the presentation $k_0[x,z]/(zf(x)-1)$ is finite, so this is a smooth curve. Its base change to $k$ is integral, as $k[x,1/f]$ is a domain, and has dimension one, so it is geometrically connected. The sheaf $\mathcal M'$ is lisse and pure of weight $v$ by hypothesis, and nonzero by Step 7. Apply [sk-l-dl-a1-energy] with $V_0=U'_0$, $N=\mathcal M'$, $B=w+2$ and $C=2(r^2+b^2)>0$, using Step 6 for every $n\ge1$. Its conclusion is $v\le B-1=(w+2)-1=w+1$.

source.place: Final paragraph: apply the trace-energy criterion

proof_origin.place: Entire proof, expanded into correction, trace bounds, Plancherel, additivity, nonvanishing and energy detection
